verdict.rationale: Sill's own Remote Access feature lets you use the Mac away from home through your own VPN (e.g. Tailscale) or a forwarded router port. It also adapts quality for slower remote links and hands the session back to the home network automatically. There is no relay, consistent with its no-server design. missing for 10: step-by-step setup docs for the VPN and port-forward paths (ports, router configuration), independent or hands-on corroboration of remote connections.

support.subject: As a power user, I can reach my machine away from home, with the relay, VPN, or port-forward path documented

citations.quote: Remote Access lets you use your Mac away from home, through your own VPN, such as Tailscale, or through a port you forward on your router.
Away from home, Sill starts at a quality a slower connection can carry, and when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself.
There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
